history.hpi: Patient was mowing his lawn approximately 30 minutes ago when he developed sudden-onset crushing substernal chest pain, 9/10, radiating to his left arm and jaw, associated with diaphoresis and nausea. Pain has not improved with rest. Denies similar pain before today.
pastMedical: Prior MI 5 years ago with drug-eluting stent placement
medications: Aspirin 81 mg daily (last dose 2 days ago, ran out)
Sildenafil (Viagra) 50 mg, taken approximately 12 hours prior to symptom onset
history.lastOralIntake: Coffee and toast approximately 2 hours ago
history.events: Wife heard him call out from the backyard and found him sitting on the ground clutching his chest, pale and sweating; she called 911 immediately

scene.dispatch: 58-year-old male, chest pain, difficulty breathing, residential backyard
scene.location: Single-family home, back yard; patient found sitting on the grass near a running lawnmower
scene.time: Saturday, mid-afternoon, 1430 hrs, warm and sunny
scene.safety: Scene is safe; mower has been shut off by a neighbor; no other hazards noted
scene.bystanders: Wife present, tearful and anxious, reports the sudden onset and that he has never had chest pain like this before
visualCues: Patient sitting on the ground, leaning forward, clutching his chest with a fist (Levine's sign)
Pale, diaphoretic skin with visible sweat on the forehead and shirt
Prescription bottle for sildenafil visible in patient's pocket when wife hands over his medications

phases.name: Initial Contact
phases.description: 58-year-old male found sitting in his backyard with acute-onset crushing chest pain radiating to the left arm and jaw, diaphoretic and anxious, pain 9/10. Vitals show sinus tachycardia and mild hypertension consistent with an acute cardiac event, though the 12-lead has not yet been acquired.

clinicalPresentation.breathing: Mildly tachypneic, equal bilateral breath sounds, no distress
clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses strong and rapid, skin pale and diaphoretic
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: It feels like an elephant is sitting on my chest... it's going into my jaw and my left arm. I feel sick.

expectedActions.shortAction: Perform rapid focused assessment; recognize signs/symptoms consistent with ACS
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Signs and symptoms include chest pain, congestive heart failure (CHF), syncope, shock, symptoms similar to a patient's previous MI
expectedActions.rationale: Early recognition drives the STEMI system of care timeline

expectedActions.shortAction: Assess cardiac rhythm; address any pulseless, symptomatic tachycardia, or symptomatic bradycardia first
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Assess the patient's cardiac rhythm and immediately address pulseless rhythms, symptomatic tachycardia, or symptomatic bradycardia
expectedActions.rationale: Rule out immediately life-threatening rhythm disturbance before proceeding

expectedActions.shortAction: Obtain complete SAMPLE history including full medication list
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: A complete medication list should be obtained from each patient. It is especially important for the treating physician and healthcare providers to be informed if the patient is taking beta-blockers, calcium channel blockers, clonidine, digoxin, blood thinners (anticoagulants), and medications for the treatment of erectile dysfunction or pulmonary hypertension
expectedActions.rationale: Sildenafil use is a critical nitrate contraindication that must be identified before NTG is considered

transitions.condition: Crew acquires and interprets a 12-lead EKG within 10 minutes of patient contact, identifying anterior ST elevation consistent with STEMI
Crew fails to acquire a 12-lead EKG within 10 minutes of patient contact, delaying STEMI recognition and hospital notification

phases.name: 12-lead acquired, STEMI Anterior recognized
phases.description: 12-lead EKG acquired within the target window shows ST-segment elevation across V1-V4 consistent with an anterior STEMI. Crew activates the STEMI system of care with advance hospital notification, gives aspirin, and establishes IV access.
phases.triggerCondition: Crew acquires a 12-lead EKG within 10 minutes of patient contact; the tracing shows significant ST-segment elevation in leads V1-V4, confirming an anterior wall STEMI.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Strong rapid radial pulses, skin pale and diaphoretic
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: Is this a heart attack? Please don't let anything happen to me.

expectedActions.shortAction: Acquire 12-lead EKG within 10 minutes of patient contact; identify STEMI
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: The 12-lead EKG is the primary diagnostic tool that identifies a STEMI; it is imperative that EMS clinicians routinely acquire a 12-lead EKG within 10 minutes for all patients exhibiting signs and symptoms of ACS
expectedActions.rationale: Meeting the 10-minute benchmark is a core STEMI performance measure

expectedActions.shortAction: Activate STEMI alert; transmit 12-lead and provide advance notification to receiving hospital
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Advance notification should be provided to the receiving hospital for patients identified as having a STEMI
expectedActions.rationale: Advance notification shortens door-to-balloon time

expectedActions.shortAction: Aspirin 324 mg PO, chewable non-enteric-coated (within 162-325 mg range)
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Administer aspirin; chewable, non-enteric-coated aspirin preferred (162–325 mg)
expectedActions.rationale: Antiplatelet therapy reduces infarct extension and mortality

expectedActions.shortAction: Establish IV access
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Establish IV access
expectedActions.rationale: Vascular access needed for medications and in case of deterioration

transitions.if: PDE5 inhibitor use identified before NTG given
transitions.condition: Crew reviews medication history, identifies sildenafil use within the past 48 hours, and correctly withholds nitroglycerin
Crew administers sublingual nitroglycerin without first screening for phosphodiesterase inhibitor use, precipitating profound hypotension

phases.name: 12-lead delayed
phases.description: Crew becomes distracted by scene management and does not acquire the 12-lead EKG within the 10-minute target window. STEMI recognition and hospital notification are delayed, prolonging total ischemic time.
phases.triggerCondition: More than 10 minutes elapse from patient contact without a 12-lead EKG being acquired; ischemic burden continues to accumulate without STEMI recognition or hospital notification.

clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: It's getting so much worse... I feel like I'm going to pass out.

expectedActions.shortAction: Immediately acquire 12-lead EKG; recognize delayed diagnosis increases morbidity/mortality risk
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Ischemic burden time is a risk for morbidity and mortality, EMS can help decrease first medical contact to intervention time/reflow by efficient scripting/training of safely minimizing scene time
expectedActions.rationale: Correct the delay as soon as recognized to limit further ischemic damage

transitions.if: STEMI recognition remains delayed, patient deteriorates
transitions.condition: STEMI goes unrecognized and untreated as ischemia progresses, precipitating ventricular fibrillation and cardiac arrest

phases.name: PDE5 use identified, NTG withheld, fentanyl given
phases.description: Crew identifies the patient's sildenafil use within the past 48 hours and correctly withholds nitroglycerin due to the risk of profound, refractory hypotension. Fentanyl is administered for ongoing severe pain.
phases.triggerCondition: Medication reconciliation reveals the patient took sildenafil approximately 12 hours ago; per protocol, nitrates are avoided and an opiate analgesic is used instead.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Strong radial pulses, skin remains diaphoretic but pain easing
otherFindings: Pain decreasing from 9/10 toward 4/10 after fentanyl
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: That's helping... the pain isn't as sharp now.

expectedActions.shortAction: Screen for PDE5 inhibitor use before considering nitroglycerin; withhold NTG given sildenafil 12 hours ago
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: The use of nitrates should be avoided in any patient who has used a phosphodiesterase inhibitor within the past 48 hours. Examples include sildenafil (Viagra®, Revatio®), vardenafil (Levitra®, Staxyn®), tadalafil (Cialis®, Adcirca®) which are used for erectile dysfunction and pulmonary hypertension
expectedActions.rationale: Nitrates combined with PDE5 inhibitors can cause severe, refractory hypotension

expectedActions.shortAction: Fentanyl 95 mcg IV for pain unresponsive to nitrates being contraindicated (95 kg × 1 mcg/kg = 95 mcg; max initial dose 100 mcg)
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Fentanyl: 1 mcg/kg IN, IM, IV or IO (maximum initial dose of 100 mcg)
expectedActions.rationale: Opiate analgesia is the appropriate alternative when nitrates are contraindicated

expectedActions.shortAction: Reassess pain score and vital signs after analgesic administration; document response
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Pain severity scores should be recorded before and after analgesic medication administration and upon arrival at destination
expectedActions.rationale: Ongoing reassessment guides need for repeat dosing and detects adverse effects

transitions.if: Pain controlled, patient stable for transport
transitions.condition: Pain improves with fentanyl, vital signs remain stable, and the patient is prepared for transport to a PCI-capable facility

phases.name: NTG given without PDE5 screen
phases.description: Nitroglycerin is given without first screening for recent PDE5 inhibitor use. Because the patient took sildenafil approximately 12 hours earlier, he develops profound, refractory hypotension requiring immediate intervention.
phases.triggerCondition: Crew administers sublingual nitroglycerin without asking about erectile dysfunction or pulmonary hypertension medications; the patient's recent sildenafil use precipitates a severe hypotensive crisis.

clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: I feel... really dizzy... everything's going dark...

expectedActions.shortAction: Recognize NTG-induced hypotension; hold further nitrates and position patient supine
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Care should always be taken when giving nitroglycerin when the patient's blood pressure is marginal. If used in this setting, the clinician should weigh the risk and benefit of nitrate administration over the administration of an opiate analgesic and be ready to respond to hypotension with fluid bolus or pressor
expectedActions.rationale: Immediate recognition prevents progression to cardiovascular collapse

expectedActions.shortAction: IV fluid bolus to treat NTG/PDE5-induced hypotension; reassess blood pressure closely
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Care should always be taken when giving nitroglycerin when the patient's blood pressure is marginal... be ready to respond to hypotension with fluid bolus or pressor
expectedActions.rationale: Fluid resuscitation is the first-line response to preload-dependent hypotension from combined NTG/PDE5 inhibitor use

phases.name: Transport to PCI center
phases.description: Pain is controlled, vital signs are stable, and serial 12-lead EKGs continue to show the anterior STEMI pattern. The patient is packaged and transported to the PCI-capable receiving facility with continued monitoring and hospital updates.
phases.triggerCondition: Analgesia is effective, hemodynamics remain stable, and the crew proceeds with transport per the regional STEMI system of care.

clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: That's a lot better, thank you. How much longer to the hospital?

expectedActions.shortAction: Perform serial 12-lead EKGs, especially with any clinical change
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Perform serial 12-lead EKGs (especially if clinical changes are noted)
expectedActions.rationale: Monitors for evolving infarct or new dysrhythmia en route

expectedActions.shortAction: Transport to appropriate PCI-capable facility per regional STEMI system of care
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Transport and destination decisions should be based on local resources and system of care
expectedActions.rationale: Timely PCI is the definitive treatment for STEMI

expectedActions.shortAction: Provide early notification to receiving facility of any condition changes or serial EKG findings
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Early notification to receiving facility of any changes in patient condition or serial EKGs
expectedActions.rationale: Keeps the receiving cath lab team updated for readiness

phases.name: STEMI progresses to VF arrest
phases.description: Prolonged, unrecognized anterior STEMI progresses to ventricular fibrillation. The patient becomes pulseless and unresponsive, requiring immediate high-quality CPR and defibrillation.
phases.triggerCondition: Delayed STEMI recognition and treatment allow ongoing myocardial ischemia to progress until the patient develops ventricular fibrillation and becomes pulseless.

expectedActions.shortAction: Recognize pulselessness; begin high-quality chest compressions immediately
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Once pulselessness is discovered, treatment should be initiated immediately, and any further history must be obtained by bystanders while treatment is ongoing
expectedActions.rationale: Minimally interrupted compressions are the most important determinant of survival

expectedActions.shortAction: Defibrillate coarse VF per biphasic protocol (e.g., Zoll 120 J, 150 J, 200 J escalating)
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Defibrillation dosing should follow manufacturer's recommendation in the case of biphasic defibrillators. If the manufacturer's recommendation is unknown, use highest setting possible. Zoll Adult – 120 J, 150 J, 200 J
expectedActions.rationale: Prompt defibrillation is the definitive treatment for VF

expectedActions.shortAction: Resume chest compressions immediately after each shock; no pause for pulse checks for 2 minutes
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Chest compressions should resume immediately after defibrillation attempts with no pauses for pulse checks for 2 minutes regardless of the rhythm displayed on the cardiac monitor
expectedActions.rationale: Interruptions in compressions reduce coronary perfusion pressure and survival

expectedActions.shortAction: Establish IV/IO access; administer Epinephrine 1 mg IV/IO during CPR
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: If feasible, IV or IO access should be obtained. Administer Epinephrine 1mg during the first or second round of compressions
expectedActions.rationale: Epinephrine supports coronary and cerebral perfusion pressure during CPR

expectedActions.shortAction: Amiodarone 300 mg IV/IO for shock-refractory VF; may repeat 150 mg in 4-6 minutes
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Amiodarone 300mg, followed by 150mg 4-6 min later if still in refractory VF and pulseless VT
expectedActions.rationale: Antiarrhythmic therapy is considered for recurrent/refractory VF
